source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_duration_ms: The experimental procedures are as follows. After the isolated brain slices were incubated in an incubator for 40 minutes, the electrophysiological activity of the brain slices gradually recovered. At this time, the stimulating electrode and the recording electrode were inserted into the hippocampal CA3 area and CA1 area pyramidal cell layer, respectively. Electrical pulses of 0.1 ms duration were delivered every 20 s. The stimulation current was gradually increased until excitatory postsynaptic potentials (EPSP) reached their maximum and remained stable. The standard stimulus intensity in the experiment was set to the intensity at which EPSP amplitude of 40% of the maximum EPSP amplitude was obtained [33]. Then the ultrasound transducer with collimator was fixed in the DG area of the hippocampus, and ultrasound gel was used for coupling. The TUS stimulation protocol used the IPIS mode with the following parameters: FF = 500 kHz, FV = 70 V, $\mathrm { N _ { F } } = 5 0 0 0 0$ , PRT = 200 ms, $\mathrm { N } _ { \mathrm { P } } ~ = ~ 3 0 0 .$ , SRT = 20 min, $\mathrm { N _ { S } } \ = \ 2 .$ . Fig. 8(a) shows the three-dimensional acoustic field distribution of the ultrasound transducer with a collimator. Fig. 8(b) and (c) plot the axial and lateral one-dimensional acoustic field distribution. The 3 dB acoustic pressure levels were 3.785 mm and 2.043 mm, respectively. The peak negative pressure value was 0.45 MPa.
